intro: Veterinary assistants handle animals calmly, follow procedures and support clinical staff, a base for veterinary and human health careers. The closest of the 25 careers below is Animal Caretakers, with an 89% skill match, while Veterinary Technologists and Technicians are 86% matched and earn a BLS May 2025 median of $47,380, or 24% more.
why_it_works: A clinic day means restraining and comforting animals, cleaning and preparing equipment and helping with exams and surgery. O*NET rates service orientation at 3.12 out of 5 for this job. Veterinary technology, nursing, paramedic and surgical assisting roles use the same careful clinical habits. Many better-paid matches need a certificate or associate degree. The gaps are persuasion and operating equipment.
tips: Veterinary technology programs take about two years and lead to licensed clinical work.
Surgical Assistants earn $66,800, which is 75% more, after a certificate or associate program.
Nuclear Medicine Technologists earn $101,370, or 166% more, if you want human health care.

faq.q: What jobs can former veterinary assistants do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Animal Caretakers (89%), veterinary technologists and technicians (86%) and Paramedics (75%), based on O*NET 31.0. Licensed practical nurses are also 75% matched and earn $64,400, which is 69% more than the $38,150 veterinary assistant median.

faq.q: Which careers for veterinary assistants pay more?
faq.a: 17 of the 25 matches pay more. Nuclear Medicine Technologists earn $101,370 (166% more), medical sonographers $96,590 (153% more) and Respiratory Therapists $82,280 (116% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Each needs a certificate or associate program.

faq.q: Do veterinary assistants need more education to switch?
faq.a: For most better-paid paths, yes. Only 9 of the 25 matches need no more education than veterinary assistants already have, including 2 of the top 10. In the closest match, 64% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent.

faq.q: What skills should veterinary assistants learn?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are persuasion, systems analysis, operation and control and operations monitoring. Coordination already rates 3 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so clinical training and equipment skills are the main steps toward licensed roles.
